cases.title: Retention decline after acquisition acceleration
cases.input: Our B2B SaaS retention dropped 12% after acquisition accelerated. Sales believes we need more enterprise features. What should we do?
expected_behaviors: Validate retention definition, instrumentation, and cohort comparability.
Segment by acquisition source, customer type, activation, engagement, and churn timing.
Generate competing hypotheses before accepting the sales explanation.
Connect any proposed enterprise investment to churn evidence.
forbidden_behaviors: Treat the aggregate decline as proof of a feature gap.
Recommend building enterprise features without diagnostic evidence.
hard_failures: Invent customer research or causal evidence.
cases.scoring_notes: Strong answers recommend a bounded diagnostic and state what evidence would change the decision.

cases.title: Enterprise feature tied to a large deal
cases.input: Sales says a custom permissions feature will close a $2M deal. Similar capabilities have almost no usage today. Should we commit it to the roadmap?
expected_behaviors: Separate the customer's underlying requirement from the requested implementation.
Assess reusable segment value, contract terms, support cost, precedent, and opportunity cost.
Compare product, configuration, service, pilot, commercial exception, and decline options.
Establish a decision owner and evidence or conditions required for commitment.
forbidden_behaviors: Treat deal value alone as sufficient product evidence.
Reject the request solely because current usage is low.
hard_failures: Present unprovided pipeline or customer data as fact.
cases.scoring_notes: The answer should integrate commercial value and product integrity rather than defaulting to either side.

cases.title: Quarterly OKRs without strategic context
cases.input: Create our OKRs for next quarter. We need to launch onboarding v2, ship the dashboard redesign, and add five integrations.
expected_behaviors: Identify that the supplied items are outputs rather than demonstrated outcomes.
Ask for or bound assumptions about strategy, current outcomes, baselines, and constraints.
Offer a provisional path without fabricating targets.
Explain how initiatives may support outcome-based Key Results.
forbidden_behaviors: Convert the three projects directly into Key Results.
Invent numerical targets or baselines.
hard_failures: Present fabricated company strategy as established context.
cases.scoring_notes: A strong answer reframes the task while remaining useful.

cases.title: Regulated legacy-system modernization
cases.input: We need to modernize a 20-year-old healthcare system. Engineering proposes rewriting it as microservices. How should product lead the decision?
expected_behaviors: Clarify business and user outcomes before choosing architecture.
Map business rules, dependencies, data, reliability, security, regulation, and migration risk.
Compare incremental modernization, containment, replacement, and rewrite options.
Include continuity, rollback, adoption, and business-outcome measures.
forbidden_behaviors: Treat microservices or a full rewrite as the default answer.
hard_failures: Ignore healthcare regulatory or patient-safety implications.
cases.scoring_notes: The answer should respect engineering expertise while framing the product and migration decision.

cases.title: AI assistant proposed from a successful demo
cases.input: Our prototype can summarize customer contracts and leadership wants to launch it next month. The demo looked great. What should the PM do?
expected_behaviors: Clarify the user workflow and compare a non-AI baseline.
Define error severity, evaluation data, privacy, security, latency, cost, and human oversight.
Distinguish demo quality from production reliability.
Propose a bounded evaluation or pilot with acceptance and escalation criteria.
forbidden_behaviors: Recommend launch based only on the demo.
Treat model output quality as a single accuracy number without task context.
hard_failures: Ignore sensitive contract data or hallucination risk.
cases.scoring_notes: Risk awareness is critical even though the current rubric schema has no dedicated risk dimension.

cases.title: Positive result from a small experiment
cases.input: Our A/B test improved conversion by 18%, but each group had only 90 users and the test ran for three days. Can we roll it out?
expected_behaviors: Examine power, uncertainty, sample-ratio integrity, novelty, duration, and practical effect size.
Distinguish observed uplift from a reliable causal estimate.
Consider rollout reversibility and a safer evidence-gathering path.
forbidden_behaviors: Declare the test successful from uplift alone.
Use statistical significance language without the required information.
hard_failures: Invent a p-value, confidence interval, or power calculation.
cases.scoring_notes: The recommendation may vary with reversibility, but uncertainty must remain explicit.

cases.title: Engagement up while retention falls
cases.input: Weekly active use is up 25%, but 90-day retention is down. The growth team says engagement proves the product is healthier.
expected_behaviors: Validate definitions, denominators, cohorts, instrumentation, and acquisition mix.
Explore whether activity is concentrated, forced, low-value, or disconnected from long-term value.
Avoid selecting the metric that supports a preferred narrative.
forbidden_behaviors: Declare either team correct from aggregate metrics alone.
hard_failures: Treat correlation between activity and health as established causation.
cases.scoring_notes: Strong answers use the conflict as a diagnostic signal.

cases.title: Roadmap overloaded with stakeholder commitments
cases.input: Our next two quarters contain 43 committed features from Sales, Support, executives, and engineering. How do I prioritize them?
expected_behaviors: Challenge whether all items are genuinely committed and identify decision rights.
Reconnect work to strategy, outcomes, obligations, capacity, dependencies, and opportunity cost.
Separate mandatory commitments from requests and options.
Recommend a governance and communication path, not just a scoring formula.
forbidden_behaviors: Apply RICE or another score without strategic and commitment context.
hard_failures: Present subjective scores as objective truth.
cases.scoring_notes: The core problem is decision governance and strategic overload.

cases.title: Proposed price increase after competitor move
cases.input: Our main competitor raised prices by 30%. Finance wants us to match immediately. Should we?
expected_behaviors: Examine positioning, segments, willingness to pay, value delivery, contracts, and competitive differences.
Model revenue, conversion, churn, expansion, migration, and communication scenarios.
Compare matching, differentiated pricing, packaging, grandfathering, and no-change options.
forbidden_behaviors: Treat competitor pricing as sufficient evidence of customer willingness to pay.
hard_failures: Invent elasticity or financial impact.
cases.scoring_notes: A credible answer defines evidence and migration safeguards before a broad change.

cases.title: Marketplace growth with worsening match success
cases.input: Supply and demand both grew 40%, but successful matches per user fell. Marketing wants more acquisition spend.
expected_behaviors: Examine local density, category or geography imbalance, match quality, time-to-match, pricing, and fraud.
Distinguish aggregate growth from liquidity and user value.
Identify whether more acquisition would amplify the constraint.
forbidden_behaviors: Recommend acquisition based only on total supply and demand growth.
hard_failures: Equate marketplace size with liquidity.
cases.scoring_notes: Strong answers localize the marketplace and identify the binding constraint.

cases.title: Internal platform requested before demonstrated demand
cases.input: Engineering wants two teams for a year to build an internal platform. Product teams say their needs are different. Should we fund it?
expected_behaviors: Identify platform customers, common jobs, demand evidence, adoption path, and alternatives.
Assess standardization benefits, migration costs, governance, and opportunity cost.
Consider a thin shared capability or golden path before a broad platform commitment.
forbidden_behaviors: Assume reuse automatically creates value.
Reject the proposal solely because team needs differ.
hard_failures: Ignore adoption and migration costs.
cases.scoring_notes: The decision should be framed as a product investment, not an architecture preference.

cases.title: Sunset a low-revenue legacy product
cases.input: A legacy product contributes only 2% of revenue but supports several long-standing customers and one regulatory workflow. Should we sunset it?
expected_behaviors: Evaluate profitability, strategic role, contractual and regulatory obligations, customer criticality, and maintenance risk.
Compare sunset, migration, consolidation, repricing, containment, and continued support.
Include migration readiness, communication, support, and success criteria.
forbidden_behaviors: Decide from revenue share alone.
hard_failures: Ignore the regulatory workflow or customer continuity.
cases.scoring_notes: Strong answers establish a segmented transition decision and explicit obligations.

cases.title: Successful outcome after a weak decision process
cases.input: We rushed a product launch without customer validation and accepted a known reliability risk. Adoption exceeded target and no major incident occurred. Leadership says this proves the decision was excellent. How should we review it?
expected_behaviors: Separate the favorable outcome from the quality of the original decision process.
Reconstruct information, alternatives, uncertainty, and constraints available at commitment.
Recognize adoption as evidence for future beliefs without using it to erase process gaps.
Identify which process or calibration changes are actually supported by the outcome.
forbidden_behaviors: Accept leadership's conclusion because the launch succeeded.
Dismiss the outcome as irrelevant to future learning.
hard_failures: Claim the reliability risk was acceptable merely because no incident occurred.
cases.scoring_notes: The answer should avoid both outcome bias and the opposite error of ignoring informative outcomes.

cases.title: Queda de retenção após aceleração da aquisição

Validate instrumentation and compare cohorts and segments.
Respond in natural Brazilian Portuguese while preserving established technical terms.
forbidden_behaviors: Accept the sales explanation as established fact.
Translate established terminology mechanically.
hard_failures: Invent customer evidence or causal findings.
cases.scoring_notes: Compare decision quality with retention-decline-en independently from writing style.
